CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake FAQ

Is CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake still on shortwave?
Yes. As of November 14, 2026, CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake is in the B-26 shortwave schedule with 132 scheduled broadcasts on 120 frequencies (4790, 5870, 5880, 5900, 6150, 6180 kHz and more). The schedule comes from EIBI and is rebuilt daily; stations can change frequencies at short notice.

What frequency is CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake on?
In the B-26 season CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake is scheduled on 120 shortwave frequencies, including 4790, 5870, 5880, 5900, 6150, 6180 kHz. Best evening option for eastern North America: 9300 kHz (4:30 pm – 12 pm Eastern). For Europe: 9300 kHz (10:30 pm – 6 pm UTC+1).

What time is CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake on shortwave?
CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake is scheduled in 55 UTC time windows this season, from 00:00–00:30 UTC through 23:45–01:15 UTC. No English broadcasts are listed this season. All times are UTC; subtract your UTC offset for local time.

Can I hear CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake in the USA?
It isn't beamed at North America this season, so hearing it in the USA is a DX catch. Your best chance is 9300 kHz (4:30 pm – 12 pm Eastern) when that band is open, or listen through an online receiver (KiwiSDR/WebSDR) closer to its target area.

Does CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake broadcast in English on shortwave?
Not this season. CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake is scheduled in Mandarin.

Is CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake on the air right now?
As of Saturday, November 14, 2026, 05:36 UTC, CNR1 Jammer/Firedrake is scheduled to be broadcasting on 6230 kHz to China. This is based on the published schedule at the time this page was built; check the live search for up-to-the-minute status.
